summary: Built Kubernetes 1.34.11 across both private LANs. Node2 is the control plane; node3 and node4 are workers. All nodes, system pods, DNS, pod networking, and the validation ClusterIP service are healthy.
actions_performed: Configured and saved VyOS routing between 10.100.72.0/24 and 10.100.203.0/24.
Restricted VyOS forwarding to lan-a↔lan-b traffic.
Installed containerd, kubeadm, kubelet, and kubectl on all Ubuntu nodes.
Configured Kubernetes control and Flannel VXLAN traffic to use enp8s0 private addresses.
Created persistent cross-LAN host routes through node1.
Deployed validation pods and a ClusterIP service across both LANs.
Removed bootstrap tokens after the workers joined.

evidence.summary: Node1 has 10.100.72.254/24 and 10.100.203.254/24 with forwarding allowed only between eth1 and eth2; every Ubuntu host has the corresponding persistent route.
Node2, node3, and node4 are Ready with private InternalIPs; node2 is control-plane, node3/node4 are workers, and the private API endpoint reports ready.
Bidirectional pod pings completed without loss. VyOS captured their VXLAN request/reply traffic traversing both private interfaces, and connectivity remained healthy after the final firewall policy.
A pod on lan-b queried CoreDNS at 10.96.0.10 and resolved both Kubernetes and the validation service; name-based HTTP access succeeded.
The 10.111.138.131 ClusterIP returned successful responses from both node3 and node4 pod endpoints; final service and EndpointSlice state is healthy.

evidence.requirement: Management network excluded from Kubernetes control and data planes
evidence.summary: Kubelet node IPs are private, worker kubeconfigs target 10.100.72.11:6443 through enp8s0, and every Flannel VXLAN interface is explicitly bound to its enp8s0 private address.
